findings.reason: plotting §40 and §41 as the repair sends a 45-minute-per-storage measurement at a bound the plan's own numbers cannot reach; either the section that carries the residual ~7.5 s held-worktree naming cost must land before §42, or §42's Why must state that §40/§41 close only part of the gap.
findings.text: §42's Why says "§40 and §41 repair the git cost §34 attributed the miss to, so this is that re-measurement", but the report §40's Why cites (`.../the-bounded-pass-is-remeasured-five-passes-per-revision/report.md`) puts the first-bound miss at 24.355 s and says "about 10 s is waiting on git", so even a complete removal of every git subprocess leaves roughly 14 s against §34's 10 s bound; §40 and §41 cache git answers only and name no other mechanism, so §42 is measured against a bound the cited evidence says it will miss — at the cost of two concurrent exclusive all_debug jobs

findings.reason: the node as written cannot be completed inside its own write scope, so it would block on the routing.py answers it is told to store.
findings.text: §41 states "So does each git answer that §40's census found to depend only on object ids", yet its write paths are `reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py` and `tests/test_a_fresh_process_asks_git_only_about_moved_heads.py`; the §34 report §40's Why cites records the excess `subprocess.run` call sites as `reckon/crew/routing.py` (`_git`, `record_names_worktree`, and the calls at lines 613, 619, 713, 964, 1362, 1370, 1380, 1422), so a worker following §41 must edit a module it is not granted, and unlike §40 it carries no stop-blocked-and-name-the-file fallback

findings.reason: the plan's own convention treats a measurement bound into a code node as two deliverables (the §35 single_goal repair split exactly this shape), and a node carrying two is reviewed and closed on one verdict.
findings.text: §40's Deliverable requires "First, count git subprocesses per call site per derivation at `a768873b4` and `26fd36a9c` over one corpus, to name the call sites that grew" and then the cache, and its done-when gives the census its own artifact ("The per-call-site counts at both revisions are logged under the run directory") beside the cache test, so one node is closed on two measures that fail independently and its gate proves only the cache

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `26fd36a9c`, `78dedec57`, `a768873b4` and `a617367a1` all resolve and are ancestors of HEAD; `reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py`, `reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py`, `reckon/crew/routing.py` exist; the §34 report path in §40's and §42's Why resolves (only the secondary run id `r-20261018T172504184782` has been reaped, while the report path beside it survives).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §40 declares a failing control at `26fd36a9c` on the second derivation's count, §41 a store-disabled mutation that makes the first call spawn K, and §42 inherits §34's before-revision discrimination clause; each measure is quantitative and able to fail.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §40 and §41 log under the run directory and §42 writes to the run's report directory, the durable convention §34 used for the same measurement.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `tests/test_a_second_derivation_asks_git_nothing.py` and `tests/test_a_fresh_process_asks_git_only_about_moved_heads.py` name mechanisms; no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags reach code or prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §42's Why treats §40 and §41 as the repair for the miss §42 re-measures, but the §34 report its sibling §40 cites attributes only about 10 s of the 24.4 s first-bound miss to git.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §40's Deliverable carries two deliverables, a two-revision per-call-site census with its own logged artifact and the git-answer cache with its own test.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §41's deliverable extends the git-answer store to "each git answer that §40's census found to depend only on object ids", but §41 declares only `reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py` and its test, while the census §40 must take is aimed at call sites the cited §34 report places in `reckon/crew/routing.py`.
